entries.appliesTo: operators that make an AI companion or AI companion platform available to users in Oregon

dutySources.disclosure-ui: § 1(2) — 'the operator shall provide on the artificial intelligence companion platform a clear and conspicuous notice that indicates that a user is interacting with artificially generated output and not a natural person'
dutySources.crisis-protocol: § 1(3)(a) — 'unless the operator has a protocol for using evidence-based methods for detecting input from the user that consists of suicidal ideation or intent or self-harm ideation or intent'
dutySources.content-safeguards: § 1(4)(a) — 'the operator shall undertake reasonable measures to prevent the artificial intelligence companion from generating statements that would lead a reasonable person to believe that the person is interacting with another natural person'

sources.scope: § 1(1)(a)(A) — 'designed to simulate a sustained, human-like platonic, intimate or romantic relationship or companionship with a user'
sources.ageFocus: § 1(3)(a) — 'An operator may not allow users in this state access to an artificial intelligence companion or artificial intelligence companion platform unless the operator has a protocol'
sources.aiDisclosure: § 1(4)(b)(B) — 'a clear and conspicuous reminder at a minimum of every three hours of interaction … along with a further reminder that the user is interacting with artificially generated output'
sources.crisisProtocol: § 1(3)(a) — 'a protocol for using evidence-based methods for detecting input from the user that consists of suicidal ideation or intent or self-harm ideation or intent and that prevents the provision of content to the user that encourages suicidal ideation, suicide or self-harm'
sources.breakReminders: § 1(4)(b)(B) — 'Provide a clear and conspicuous reminder at a minimum of every three hours of interaction that the user should take a break'
sources.engagementLimits: § 1(4)(c)(A) — 'a system of rewards or affirmations with the purpose of reinforcing behavior or maximizing the time during which the user engages with the artificial intelligence companion'
sources.contentSafeguards: § 1(4)(a)(A)–(D) — 'Explicitly claim that the artificial intelligence companion is sentient or human; … Simulate romantic interest or are sexual innuendo; or … Role-play romantic relationships between adults and minors'
sources.penaltyMax: § 2(1)(a) — 'The greater of the individual's actual damages or statutory damages of $1,000 for each violation'
sources.enforcer: § 2(1) — 'An individual who suffers an ascertainable loss of money or property or other injury in fact as a result of an operator's violation of section 1 of this 2026 Act may bring an action in a court of this state'

flags: ageFocus coded all-users (disclosure § 1(2) and crisis protocol § 1(3) bind for all users) but § 1(4) adds minor-specific safeguards triggered by a 'knows or has reason to believe … is a minor' knowledge standard — no age-verification duty imposed, so age-assurance not assigned and ageThreshold omitted (text never defines 'minor' numerically)
aiDisclosure coded periodic from the minors-only three-hour reminder (§ 1(4)(b)(B)); the general § 1(2) notice states no timing — lossy
annual public transparency report (§ 1(5): post referral counts and protocol details on a publicly accessible website by December 31 each year) and protocol publication (§ 1(3)(c)) fit no listed duty
§ 1(3)(b)(A) allows an alternative youthline referral for users the operator identifies as under 25 years of age

§ 1(4)(c)(B)–(C) also prohibits guilt/abandonment messages on disengagement and material misrepresentations about the companion's identity, capabilities or training data — coded under engagementLimits/contentSafeguards

exposure: statutory damages are 'the greater of the individual's actual damages or statutory damages of $1,000 for each violation'; injunction and attorney fees/costs also available (§ 2(1)(b), § 2(2)); no agency enforcement provision
